In January 2021, GameStop's stock rose about 2,700% in under three weeks. Then it fell more than 86%.

Per the SEC's staff report (Oct 2021), GameStop short interest reached 122.97% of its float in January 2021. As online investors piled in, the stock closed at $347.51 on Jan 27 and hit $483 intraday on Jan 28, up about 2,700% from its Jan 8 intraday low, and some brokers restricted trading. The SEC found buying by short sellers was a small fraction of buy volume: positive sentiment sustained the rise. Then the price fell more than 86%. Prices as reported in 2021. Past results don't guarantee future ones.

youtube_description:
The SEC staff report on early 2021 market conditions (Oct 2021) found GameStop's intraday price rose about 2,700% from its Jan 8, 2021 low to its Jan 28 high of $483, after closing at $347.51 on Jan 27, followed by a decrease of over 86%. Short interest reached 122.97% of float in January 2021, but the SEC found buying by short sellers was a small fraction of buy volume and that positive sentiment sustained the rise. Prices as reported in 2021. Past results don't guarantee future ones. Education only, not financial advice. AI narration.
